### Step 1 — Scene
A breakfast tray with two fried eggs, two slices of toast, two muffins, coffee, and orange juice. I include the side plate because it is clearly part of this tray, rather than an unrelated plate at the image edge.

### Step 2 — Vessels
- Main plate: approximately **26 cm** diameter; area **531 cm²**.
- Muffin side plate: approximately **20 cm** diameter; area **314 cm²**.
- Coffee mug and juice glass: estimated from their visible fill levels.

### Steps 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
The eggs have a slight sheen, but no separately measurable pool of oil; their energy estimate includes frying fat.

| Item | Vessel area covered | Area × average height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Two toast slices | 40% of main plate | 212 cm² × 1.0 cm = 212 ml | 0.30 | 64 g | 270 | 173 kcal |
| Two fried eggs | 29% of main plate | 154 cm² × 0.7 cm = 108 ml | 1.0 | 108 g | 195 | 211 kcal |
| Two muffins | 42% of side plate | 132 cm² × 3.0 cm = 396 ml | 0.38 | 150 g | 350 | 525 kcal |
| Coffee, apparently with some milk | — | Approximately 240 ml | 1.0 | 240 g | 15 | 36 kcal |
| Orange juice | — | Approximately 180 ml | 1.04 | 187 g | 45 | 84 kcal |

**Area check:** food covers approximately **69% of the main plate** and **42% of the side plate**, consistent with the visible empty space. Muffin density accounts for their airy crumb; no additional volume reduction is applied.

Two sealed spread portions are also visible, but their contents and amounts cannot be established confidently, so they are excluded.

### Step 8 — Sanity check
Estimated solid food: **322 g and 909 kcal**. Including drinks: **749 g and approximately 1,030 kcal**. This is plausible for two muffins, toast, eggs, and two drinks; muffin size and recipe are the largest uncertainties.
